detail.readme:
### Paradev The open-source workspace for Claude Code, Codex, and any coding agent. **Download:** [**macOS**](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest)  •  [**Linux**](https://paradev.com/download)  •  [**iOS**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6788926383)  •  [**Android**](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.paradev.mobile) [Documentation](https://docs.paradev.com)  •  [Changelog](https://paradev.com/changelog)  •  [Discord](https://discord.gg/cZeD9WYcV7) [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/paradevai/paradev?style=flat&logo=github)](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/stargazers) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue?style=flat)](LICENSE.md)
## Why Paradev Paradev is the workspace for running parallel coding agents. You can run any coding agent, like Claude Code or Codex. - **Agents run in parallel and never touch each other's files.** Every task gets its own worktree, branch, and terminal. - **Run on your laptop, in the cloud, or on a remote machine.** Closing your laptop doesn't kill your agents. - **Agents can drive it too.** Our CLI, MCP server, and skills let agents drive the entire app and orchestrate other agents. - **Check in from anywhere** with our mobile and web apps. - **View Git changes right in the app.** Read the diff, check the pull request, and merge without leaving. - **Use the agents you already have.** Paradev runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Cursor Agent, and any other CLI agent on the plans and API keys you already have, in a terminal or as a chat. ## Get started 1. **Download the app.** - macOS: [Apple Silicon (.dmg)](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Paradev-arm64.dmg) · [Intel (.dmg)](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Paradev-x64.dmg) - Linux: [x64 AppImage](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/releases/latest/download/Paradev-x86_64.AppImage) (experimental) - Windows: not yet available 2. **Add a repository** from your computer, or clone one. 3. **Create a workspace**, choose your CLI agent, and describe a small change. 4. **Review the result** in **Changes**, run the tests, and preview your app in the browser pane before you commit. You need [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and at least one coding agent you already use. [gh](https://cli.github.com/) is optional and enables the pull request workflows; Paradev offers to install it for you. For a full walkthrough, see [Your First Parallel Session](https://docs.paradev.com/first-workspace). The `superset` CLI comes with the desktop app. You can also install it on its own: ```bash curl -fsSL https://paradev.com/cli/install.sh | sh # or brew install paradevai/tap/superset ``` Paradev was previously named Superset, so the command is still `superset`. It is unrelated to Apache Superset, the business intelligence tool. ## Features
### Parallel workspaces Every agent runs in its own Git worktree and branch, keeping working files separate. Try two approaches to one problem and keep the better one. Changes can still conflict when merged, and worktrees do not sandbox processes. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/workspaces)
### Agent status Track every agent from the sidebar. You get working indicators, a chime when an agent finishes, and a dock badge when one needs your attention. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-integration)
### Review and pull requests Inspect, comment on, and edit agent changes in the diff viewer. Select diff lines to send feedback to an agent. Then watch the PR checks and merge without leaving the app. [Diff viewer →](https://docs.paradev.com/diff-viewer) · [Pull requests →](https://docs.paradev.com/pull-requests)
### In-app browser Preview your dev server next to your terminals, on the ports Paradev detects for each workspace. Turn on Design, click the part of the page you want to change, and describe the change to an agent. Your agent can click through the page and check its own work. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/browser)
### Automations Run agents on a schedule or when something happens: a review request, a Slack message, a Linear issue, a Sentry issue, or a webhook. Each run opens a workspace you can review and continue. Automations need the Pro plan. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/automations)
### Cloud workspaces Each workspace gets its own cloud machine and keeps working when your laptop is closed. Check in from desktop, iOS, or Android. Cloud workspaces are included with Team and Ultra. [Docs →](https://docs.paradev.com/cloud-workspaces) · [Learn more →](https://paradev.com/cloud)
### iOS and Android Start agents, follow them live, and review the diff on iOS or Android. You can also merge the pull request there. The app is included with Paradev Pro. The iOS app requires iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later. [App Store →](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6788926383) · [Google Play →](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.paradev.mobile) · [Learn more →](https://paradev.com/mobile)
### CLI, SDK, and MCP server Drive the entire app and cloud from the CLI, the SDK, or over MCP. Create workspaces, start agents, and read their terminals from a shell, a TypeScript program, or another agent. [CLI →](https://docs.paradev.com/cli/getting-started) · [SDK →](https://docs.paradev.com/sdk/getting-started) · [MCP →](https://docs.paradev.com/mcp-server)
More in the docs: [remote access](https://docs.paradev.com/remote-access) (Pro plan) · [Pages](https://docs.paradev.com/pages) · [plugins](https://docs.paradev.com/plugins/overview) · [terminal](https://docs.paradev.com/terminal-integration) · [terminal scripts](https://docs.paradev.com/terminal-scripts) · [setup scripts](https://docs.paradev.com/setup-teardown-scripts) · [skills](https://docs.paradev.com/skills) · [Linear](https://docs.paradev.com/use-with-linear) and [Slack](https://docs.paradev.com/use-with-slack) (Pro plan) · [open in your IDE](https://docs.paradev.com/use-with-ide) · [model providers](https://docs.paradev.com/providers) · [themes](https://docs.paradev.com/custom-themes) · [shortcuts](https://docs.paradev.com/keyboard-shortcuts) · compare with [Cursor](https://paradev.com/compare/cursor-alternative), the [Codex app](https://paradev.com/compare/codex-app-alternative), and [Conductor](https://paradev.com/compare/conductor-alternative) ## Supported agents Use the agent plans and API keys you already have. These agents are built in, and you can add any other CLI agent with its own icon. Integration depth varies: some agents report status, resume after a restart, and appear on the Usage page. See [supported agents](https://docs.paradev.com/supported-agents) for the full table.  [Amp Code](https://ampcode.com/)  ·   [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/)  ·   [Claude Code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code)  ·   [OpenAI Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex)  ·   [Cursor Agent](https://docs.cursor.com/agent)  ·   [Droid](https://www.factory.ai/)  ·   [fx](https://fx.sh/)  ·   [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)  ·   [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot)  ·   [Grok](https://x.ai/)  ·   [Hermes](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent)  ·   [Muse Code](https://developer.meta.com/ai/products/muse-code/)  ·   [Devin](https://devin.ai/cli)  ·   [Kimi Code](https://www.kimi.com/)  ·   [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/cli/)  ·   [Mastra Code](https://mastra.ai/)  ·   [Mistral Vibe](https://mistral.ai/)  ·   [Oh My Pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)  ·   [OpenCode](https://github.com/opencode-ai/opencode)  ·   [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono/tree/main/packages/coding-agent)  ·   [Polygraph](https://trypolygraph.com/)
FAQ
Is Paradev a terminal app or a desktop app?
Paradev is a desktop app, not a terminal app. Agents run inside it as a chat or in a terminal. Next to them you get a diff viewer, pull requests, an in-app browser, and a file editor. [FAQ docs](https://docs.paradev.com/faq)
Do I have to use a terminal, or can I chat with the coding agent?
No, Paradev can show an agent session as a chat instead of a terminal, and you approve or decline the agent's actions with a click. Chat works with Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi; Paradev runs the CLI you already installed, so it keeps your login and settings. The **CLI** / **Chat** toggle switches a running session without losing context, and other agents run in a Paradev terminal. [Chat docs](https://docs.paradev.com/chat)
What is the Paradev license, what does it cost, and which platforms does it run on?
Paradev is open source under the MIT License. The Free plan covers local workspaces with the desktop app and the CLI. Paid plans add features such as automations and cloud workspaces. The desktop app runs on macOS, with an experimental Linux AppImage; Windows is not available yet. [Pricing](https://paradev.com/pricing) · [FAQ docs](https://docs.paradev.com/faq)
Is Paradev the same as Superset? Is it related to Apache Superset?
Paradev was previously named Superset, which is why the CLI command is still `superset`. It is not related to Apache Superset, the business intelligence tool. [Install docs](https://docs.paradev.com/install)
Which coding agents does Paradev support, and do I keep my own subscriptions?
Paradev has built-in support for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Gemini CLI, Amp, and more, and you can add any other CLI agent. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi can also run as a chat. Agents use your own subscriptions and API keys, and Paradev does not proxy model calls. [Supported agents docs](https://docs.paradev.com/supported-agents)
How do I keep multiple coding agents from overwriting each other in one repository?
Paradev gives each agent its own workspace: a Git worktree on its own branch, with its own terminal. Agents edit separate copies of the working files, so one agent does not overwrite another agent's changes. Worktrees do not sandbox processes, and branches can still conflict when you merge them. [Workspaces docs](https://docs.paradev.com/workspaces)
I have too many Claude Code terminal sessions. How do I keep track of them?
Paradev shows every agent session in one sidebar, grouped by project, with a status for each, whether the session runs as a chat or in a terminal. Claude Code reports when it finishes and when it waits for your input, and the sidebar flags workspaces that need you. [Agent status docs](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-status)
Can I run two coding agents on the same task and compare the results?
Yes, in Paradev you give the same prompt to two or more workspaces, each on its own branch, with the same agent or different agents. You then compare the diffs and keep the best result. [Race agents recipe](https://docs.paradev.com/recipes/race-agents)
Can I use Claude Code and Codex together, with one writing code and the other reviewing it?
Yes, Paradev runs Claude Code and Codex side by side, each as a chat or in a terminal. To get a review, select lines in a pull request's **Code** tab and send them to the other agent, or use **Continue with another agent** to start a session of a different agent with the recent context. [Agent sessions docs](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-sessions)
How do I review a coding agent's diff and send follow-ups before I merge?
Paradev shows each workspace's changes in a diff viewer, where you commit, push, and open a pull request. In the pull request's **Code** tab, select lines and send a comment to a running agent or a new session; posting it to GitHub is optional. You can watch the checks and merge from the same view. [Pull requests docs](https://docs.paradev.com/pull-requests)
How do I keep each branch's dev server, ports, and preview apart?
Paradev keeps each branch in its own worktree and shows the ports that each workspace's processes listen on, grouped by workspace. Select a port to open that branch's dev server in the in-app browser. Paradev does not assign port ranges, so set per-workspace config in a setup script, which runs in each new workspace with variables such as `SUPERSET_WORKSPACE_PATH`. [Ports docs](https://docs.paradev.com/ports)
Can I click an element in my running web app and have a coding agent change it?
Yes, Paradev has a Design mode in its in-app browser: open your dev server, turn on **Design**, and click the element. You then describe the change, and the agent gets the element's details and a screenshot with your note. [Browser docs](https://docs.paradev.com/browser)
Can I get notified when a coding agent needs my input?
Yes, the Paradev desktop app notifies you when an agent finishes or stops to wait for your input, and the macOS dock icon shows a badge. Support varies by agent: Claude Code reports both states, and some agents report only when they finish. On the mobile app, a dot on the workspace shows that an agent needs your permission; push notifications are not available yet. [Agent status docs](https://docs.paradev.com/agent-status)
Can I check on my coding agents and answer them from my phone?
Yes, Paradev for iOS and Android lets you start agents, follow their sessions live, answer them, and review their changes. It needs Paradev Pro. Get it on the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/id6788926383) (iOS 26 or iPadOS 26 or later) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.paradev.mobile). For workspaces on your computer, turn on Remote Access and keep the computer awake and online. [Mobile app docs](https://docs.paradev.com/mobile)
Can a coding agent run on a schedule, like nightly maintenance or a weekly flaky-test check?
Yes, Paradev automations run an agent on an hourly, daily, weekly, or custom schedule. Each run creates a workspace where you review the changes and continue the work. Automations need the Pro plan. [Automations docs](https://docs.paradev.com/automations)
Can I start a coding agent from Slack, Linear, Sentry, or a GitHub pull request?
Yes, Paradev automations start an agent when a GitHub pull request event, a Slack message, a Linear issue, a Sentry issue, or a webhook arrives, and the agent gets the event details with your prompt. You can also mention the Paradev bot in Slack to start a cloud workspace and agent. Automations and the Slack integration need the Pro plan. [Automations docs](https://docs.paradev.com/automations)
Can I start coding agents from the command line or from another agent?
Yes, the Paradev CLI creates workspaces and starts agents in them from a shell script or from another agent. Agents can also use the Paradev MCP server to work with workspaces and terminals. The desktop app includes an orchestrate skill that lets one agent coordinate workers in separate workspaces. [CLI docs](https://docs.paradev.com/cli/getting-started)
Can I run coding agents on a remote machine or in the cloud and review the changes from my laptop?
Yes, with Paradev remote access (Pro plan) you open workspaces hosted on another machine, such as a Mac mini or a server, from your laptop. Cloud workspaces (Team and Ultra plans) run each workspace on its own cloud machine, so agents keep working when your laptop is closed. [Remote access docs](https://docs.paradev.com/remote-access)
Can I come back to a task later with its agent session and branch still there?
Yes, a Paradev workspace stays on disk as a Git worktree on its branch until you delete it. Terminals belong to a background process, so they keep running and keep their scrollback when you close or update the app. If a terminal stops after a crash or restart, Paradev can resume the agent session for agents that support resume, such as Claude Code and Codex. [Keep agents running docs](https://docs.paradev.com/keep-agents-running)
Can a small team share one machine for coding agents?
Yes, a Paradev host can be a shared machine, such as a Mac mini, that teammates reach through remote access (Pro plan). When the host first comes online, only the person who started it has access. That person adds teammates under **Settings → Hosts**. [Remote access docs](https://docs.paradev.com/remote-access)
How is Paradev different from Conductor, Orca, and Cursor?
Paradev, Conductor, and Orca all run coding agents in parallel Git worktrees, and Cursor is an AI editor built around its own agent. Paradev runs any CLI agent on your own subscriptions, and it opens a workspace in Cursor when you want to edit there. Orca is also open source and runs on Windows, which Paradev does not support yet. Conductor is joining Meta and is closed to new users, and Paradev has a guide to move Conductor workspaces over. [Migrate from Conductor](https://docs.paradev.com/migrate-from-conductor)
Is Paradev a replacement for tmux?
Yes, for running coding agents Paradev can replace tmux: its terminal sessions keep running when you close, quit, or update the app. Each workspace also gets its own worktree and status in the sidebar. You can still run tmux inside a Paradev terminal. [Keep agents running docs](https://docs.paradev.com/keep-agents-running)
## Contributing Clone the repository, add it to the installed Paradev app, and create a workspace for your change. Then run the setup script once in that workspace terminal: ```bash ./.paradev/setup.local.sh bun run dev ``` The script starts local Postgres and Redis with Docker and seeds a dev account. You do not need third-party credentials. See [DEVELOPMENT.md](./DEVELOPMENT.md) for the prerequisites and the full guide, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to open a pull request. ## Community - **[Star this repo](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev)**: we ship every day, and a star lets you follow along - **[Discord](https://discord.gg/cZeD9WYcV7)**: chat with the team and community - **[X](https://x.com/paradevai)**: follow for updates and announcements - **[GitHub Issues](https://github.com/paradevai/paradev/issues)**: report bugs and request features - **Docs for agents**: [a Markdown index](https://docs.paradev.com/llms.txt) or [one full-text file](https://docs.paradev.com/llms-full.txt) [![Avi on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Avi-@avimakesrobots-555?logo=x)](https://x.com/avimakesrobots) [![Kiet on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kiet-@flyakiet-555?logo=x)](https://x.com/flyakiet) [![Satya on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Satya-@saddle__paddle-555?logo=x)](https://x.com/saddle_paddle)

## License and pricing The Free plan covers local workspaces, the desktop app, and the CLI, with no credit card required. Paid plans are optional: the [Pro plan](https://paradev.com/pricing) adds remote access, automations, the iOS and Android apps, and the Linear and Slack integrations, and the Team and Ultra plans add cloud workspaces. Paradev is open source under the [MIT License](LICENSE.md). You can inspect, modify, and self-host it, and anyone can file issues, open pull requests, or fork it.
